transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-14
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Aurora Partnerships), Marcus Li (Aurora Cloud Eng), Ravi Menon (Aurora GPU Lead)
Recording link: (redacted)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): quick partner intro + tech discovery, discuss pilot and benchmarks, security checklist requested

00:00:02 Sofia Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood Inference, and with me is Diego our systems engineer. how are you all doing?
00:00:12 Lena Park: good, thanks. excited to chat - been looking forward to this one.
00:00:16 Marcus Li: morning all, thanks for making time.
00:00:20 Diego Martinez: hey! quick note, apologies if you hear some keyboard clatter, I'm on a bit of a call stack here.

00:01:05 Sofia Chen: quick agenda - intro to Redwood partner program, short tech overview, we want to understand Aurora's infra and partnership goals, then discuss pilot/next steps. does that work?
00:01:18 Ravi Menon: sounds good. we're curious about how Redwood routes between hosted and dedicated, and what you'd expect from a partner integration.

00:02:10 Sofia Chen: yes great. at a high level Redwood is a developer-first inference platform - hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments for VPC/on-prem. we do model routing, KV cache, batching, cost controls, etc. for partners we typically focus on joint go-to-market, co-branded reference archs, and technical integrations for private deployments.
00:02:33 Marcus Li: when you say private deployments, do you mean we run a control plane in your cloud or we run the full stack in our VPC?
00:02:40 Diego Martinez: good question - we have two patterns. one is a private control plane where the control signals are in Redwood but workloads stay in customer VPC, the other is a full on-prem-ish package where customers run the entire control plane and inference runtime internally. both support KMS/HSM and audit logs.
00:03:05 Lena Park: okay, we definitely have customers that need full data residency options so the second model is interesting.

00:03:40 Sofia Chen: can you tell us about Aurora's GPU fleet? what models, approximate node counts, and whether you do preemptible/burst offerings?
00:03:52 Ravi Menon: sure - currently we have a mix: about 120 A100 80GB nodes and ~40 H100 nodes in our primary region. we also run some older A40 ish instances for less critical workloads. we offer reserved pools to customers and a spot-like burst pool.
00:04:12 Marcus Li: on network we use VPC with direct connect to a few enterprise customers, and we can provide private peering.

00:04:45 Diego Martinez: nice, that H100 count is helpful. for Redwood Dedicated we'd provision a reserved GPU pool and we can autoscale for burst. curious about your NVLink / multi-GPU configs - are these single-socket nodes or DGX style with full NVLink?
00:05:05 Ravi Menon: currently single-socket A100/H100 nodes, no DGX clusters. we do have plans to pilot multi-GPU interconnect in Q1.

00:05:30 Sofia Chen: perfect. typical partner integrations: we map routes by policy (latency, cost), so if you want to be a capacity partner for Dedicated we can route eligible requests to your pool. there's also model variant compatibility to consider - quantization and kernel selection. sometimes names come through funky in transcripts, we call KV cache but AirPods thinks 'KV cash' so forgive the noise,
00:05:56 Marcus Li: (laughs) all good. how do you handle client auth for private endpoints? SSO? tokens?
00:06:05 Diego Martinez: we support mTLS for service-to-service, token-based API keys for customers, and SAML/SSO for the console side. for private deployments we can integrate with customer IdP and use short-lived certs.

00:06:35 Lena Park: any SOC2 or ISO certifications currently? our procurement team will ask.
00:06:40 Sofia Chen: Redwood's hosted API is SOC2 Type II, and we have an enterprise compliance package for Private deployments that includes audit logs, KMS integration, and contractual commitments. we'll share the security pack.

00:07:20 Marcus Li: great. on pricing - if we were to be a capacity partner, is it revenue share, referral, or fixed capacity?
00:07:28 Sofia Chen: typical portfolio: for partners we do a referral fee for customers we route, or a revenue share for dedicated pools, and in some cases a fixed committed capacity model. economics depend on region and SLA. we'll put sample numbers in the partner playbook.

00:08:02 Ravi Menon: we'd want to see latency numbers - for low-latency chat features our customers need under 200ms tail. can Redwood meet that on external routing?
00:08:15 Diego Martinez: typical latencies depend on model size and sequence length. for smaller open models we hit low-ms but larger 70B-ish models can be higher. we use batching and KV prefix caching to reduce per-token cost but keep latency SLOs. for Dedicated you can get pinned capacity which helps tail latency.

00:08:50 Marcus Li: do you do inference kernels optimized for H100? we heard some runtimes don't utilize the newer tensorcores well.
00:08:58 Diego Martinez: yes we tune kernels per architecture. we do a compile step to select kernels and optimize for sequence length distribution. however sometimes community model forks need tweaks. we'll run a short benchmark on your H100 to validate.

00:09:30 Lena Park: from a go-to-market angle, we have an enterprise sales channel and a self-serve developer portal. what's the easiest partner path? integrations in the console?
00:09:42 Sofia Chen: many partners start with a referral + technical validation pilot. we can put you on the partner registry, joint marketing, and a referral flow. If you want integration into our console for direct provisioning, that's a deeper product integration which we can scope.

00:10:15 Marcus Li: regarding network egress and data residency - do you route customer data through Redwood when using you as a capacity partner?
00:10:25 Diego Martinez: policy-based routing can keep payloads in your region. For private control plane we try to avoid payload egress: the inference happens in your VPC. For dedicated pools we can set region constraints. we also support customer-managed KMS.

00:11:05 Ravi Menon: interesting. what's your onboarding timeline for a partner pilot?
00:11:10 Sofia Chen: typically 2-4 weeks to stand up a pilot if we have node access and basic networking. a deeper private deployment can take 4-8 weeks depending on compliance and legal.

00:11:40 Marcus Li: legal - we need to review SLA terms and indemnity. Lena will own that.
00:11:45 Lena Park: yep I'll loop in legal once we have the playbook.

00:12:10 Diego Martinez: can you share a rough QPS profile and model mix for workloads you expect to route to Redwood? e.g., percent of requests 1-2 tokens vs long generation?
00:12:22 Marcus Li: right now our customers are mostly generation for summarization and chat - maybe 30% short calls under 50 tokens, 50% 50-200 tokens, and 20% longform. QPS varies by tenant.

00:12:50 Diego Martinez: perfect, that distribution helps for batching policy recommendations. we'll recommend some quantization profiles for A100 vs H100.

00:13:25 Lena Park: any concerns around multi-tenancy and noisy neighbors? our customers will want predictable performance per tenant.
00:13:33 Sofia Chen: that's exactly what Redwood Dedicated is for - reserved GPU pools, per-tenant isolation, and autoscaling for bursts. plus we offer trace-level visibility in Redwood Console so you can see token-level cost and latency.

00:13:55 Marcus Li: demo request - Diego, would you be open to running a small benchmark on our H100 cluster with a sample 13B and 70B open model to show latency/cost?
00:14:08 Diego Martinez: absolutely. we'll need SSH access to a sample node, GPU driver details, and a Docker runtime we can run. we'll provide a runbook.
00:14:20 Ravi Menon: drivers are standard NVIDIA 535, CUDA 12, containerd. we can provide an SSH key and a staging node.

00:14:40 Sofia Chen: perfect. next on security - do you have customer-managed KMS?
00:14:46 Marcus Li: yes, we can expose KMS for tenant keys via HSM and have audit logs.
00:14:52 Diego Martinez: great, that'll map to our private deployment option easily.

00:15:30 Sofia Chen: quick note - sometimes transcripts auto change product names; when I say 'Redwood Dedicated' it might appear as 'Redwood Dedicate' in the export, so just ignore small typos.

00:16:10 Lena Park: one slightly nitty-gritty question: can you support custom model onboarding? a lot of our SI partners bring custom fine-tuned models and they want to serve them.
00:16:20 Diego Martinez: yes we support custom model onboarding. We have a model catalog process and secure model artifact ingestion. for larger models we provide quantization suggestions and kernel tuning. there may be additional support cost for heavy engineering.

00:17:00 Marcus Li: what telemetry do you require from our side to run the benchmarks? we prefer minimal ops changes.
00:17:07 Diego Martinez: ideally an SSH endpoint, a small container runtime, and network egress to our bench controller. we can run everything containerized so it's low-friction.

00:17:35 Sofia Chen: commercial question - would Aurora prefer to be a capacity partner where we route customers programmatically, or more of a referral partner?
00:17:44 Lena Park: we prefer to start as referral + pilot. if the pilot shows good economics and SLA alignment we can consider capacity partnership.

00:18:05 Sofia Chen: sounds like a plan. we'll propose pilot scope: 2-week benchmark on H100 and A100, validation of tail latency for a 13B and a 70B, and then a joint go-to-market plan if results look good.

00:18:22 Marcus Li: timeline wise we can provision a staging H100 node by 2026-12-17.

00:18:28 Sofia Chen: perfect. Diego, can you own the bench run?
00:18:32 Diego Martinez: yes I'll own it. I'll draft the runbook and share by Friday.

00:18:50 Ravi Menon: one more question on billing flow - if we are capacity partner and traffic is routed through Redwood does billing happen through Redwood or directly invoiced to Aurora?
00:19:02 Sofia Chen: normally Redwood invoices the end customer and we handle revenue share with partners, but we can do partner-billed models with contractual adjustments. we'll put options in the playbook.

00:19:35 Lena Park: procurement will want to see SOC2 + pen test reports.
00:19:40 Sofia Chen: we'll attach the security pack.

00:20:10 Diego Martinez: any existing integrations you have with other inference runtimes? i.e., are customers already using Lambda or Paperspace as their inferencing tier?
00:20:20 Marcus Li: we've had some customers using Lambda and some using cloud provider managed endpoints. many are still evaluating.

00:20:45 Sofia Chen: ok. high-level technical deep dive request: after we run the bench we'd like a follow-up meeting with your infra folks to review kernel-level tuning and network topology.
00:20:56 Marcus Li: agreed. let's schedule that for the week of 12/21.

00:21:30 Lena Park: are there any regulatory constraints you commonly see from customers? we have some EU-based clients asking about data residency.
00:21:38 Sofia Chen: yes EU data residency and GDPR concerns are common - we support region pinning and private deployments to keep data local, plus contractual guarantees for data handling.

00:22:05 Marcus Li: good. on the partnership margins, do you publish partner rates or is it bespoke?
00:22:12 Sofia Chen: we have a partner rate card and a few bespoke options for large commitments. we'll include sample economics in the playbook.

00:22:40 Ravi Menon: logistic Q: what level of SRE support do you provide during pilot runs?
00:22:47 Diego Martinez: Redwood SE will support the benchmark run, and for pilots we provide SRE on-call during business hours; enterprise customers can get extended coverage.

00:23:20 Lena Park: okay - if we're aligned on pilot scope I can introduce legal and partnerships to your commercial lead.
00:23:28 Sofia Chen: great - we'll include an intro to our commercial lead in the partner playbook.

00:24:05 Marcus Li: any limitations on models we can serve? e.g., closed-source restrictions or export controls?
00:24:13 Diego Martinez: we enforce export controls and do blacklist checks; some models with licensing restrictions may need special handling but generally we can serve customer-owned models.

00:24:45 Sofia Chen: quick recap so we have alignment: 1) Redwood to share partner playbook and security pack (Sofia), 2) Redwood SE to share benchmark runbook and spreadsheet (Diego), 3) Aurora to provision staging H100 node and provide inventory (Marcus/Ravi), 4) schedule technical deep dive week of 12/21, 5) procurement/legal to get security docs (Lena).
00:25:12 Lena Park: yep that matches our view.

00:25:30 Sofia Chen: any final questions from Aurora?
00:25:35 Marcus Li: none from me. one small asks: can Redwood support our white-label offering in console? some customers want co-branded UIs.
00:25:45 Sofia Chen: we have some API hooks and console customization for partners; deeper white-labeling is possible but would be scoped as part of an integration project. we can add that to the follow-up scope.

00:26:05 Diego Martinez: i'll jot that down - console customization as an optional deliverable.

00:26:40 Sofia Chen: ok if no more questions we'll look to wrap and confirm next steps. thanks for the time today.
00:26:50 Lena Park: thanks Sofia, thanks Diego. excited to move forward.
00:26:55 Marcus Li: thanks all.
